en: Udāna 8.3 Tatiyanibbānapaṭisaṁyuttasutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion the Blessed One was instructing, exhorting, inspiring, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk concerning Nibbāna.
And those bhikkhus were listening to the Dhamma with eager ears, attending to it with their whole mind, and applying their whole heart to it.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
"There is, monks, an unborn, an unbecome, an unmade, an unconditioned.

If, monks, there were not this unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, an escape from the born, the become, the made, the conditioned would not be discerned here. But because there is an unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, therefore an escape from the born, the become, the made, the conditioned is discerned."
"But because, monks, there is the unborn, the unbecome, the unmade, the unconditioned, therefore an escape from the born, the become, the made, the conditioned is discerned.
